# OuroProvider

Optional app-level provider that routes internal `href`s through your router's link and groups tooltips: once one `Tooltip` shows, its neighbours open instantly instead of each waiting its own delay. Ouro UI components work without it: they honor reduced motion themselves, in CSS (`motion-reduce:` variants and `prefers-reduced-motion` queries), and need no animation library. If your app animates with Motion, wrap it in `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="user">` for the same behavior.

```tsx
import { OuroProvider } from "@/registry/ouro/lib/ouro/ouro-provider";
```

## Example

```tsx
// React Router. app/components/ouro-router-link.tsx:
import type { ComponentProps } from "react";
import { Link } from "react-router";
import type { OuroLinkComponent } from "@/lib/ouro/use-ouro";

export function OuroRouterLink({ href, ...props }: ComponentProps<OuroLinkComponent>) {
  return <Link to={href} {...props} />;
}

// app/root.tsx:
import { Outlet } from "react-router";
import { OuroProvider } from "@/lib/ouro/ouro-provider";
import { OuroRouterLink } from "@/components/ouro-router-link";

export default function App() {
  return (
    <OuroProvider linkComponent={OuroRouterLink}>
      <Outlet />
    </OuroProvider>
  );
}

// Next.js App Router. app/providers.tsx:
"use client";

import Link from "next/link";
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { OuroProvider } from "@/lib/ouro/ouro-provider";

export function Providers({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return <OuroProvider linkComponent={Link}>{children}</OuroProvider>;
}

// app/layout.tsx, a Server Component:
import type { ReactNode } from "react";
import { Providers } from "./providers";

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en">
      <body>
        <Providers>{children}</Providers>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

## Usage

An app with a motion setting of its own passes it as `motion`: `<OuroProvider motion={still ? "reduced" : "system"}>`. Its springs, scrolls and moving pictures then follow the app's setting, and your components can too, through `useReducedMotion()`.

It installs with every component that renders links (`Button`, `Link`, `Card`, `Item`, `Table` and the navigation components) and with `Tooltip`. An app with none of those adds it by name, `lib-ouro-provider`, at the release tag of your other components (the README's Next.js steps show the command). Type a custom adapter with `ComponentProps<OuroLinkComponent>` so it always compiles, including under `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`.

Every Ouro UI link takes `href`: `Link`, `Button`, `Card`, `Item` and `Table` rows. An internal `href` (a path) renders through `linkComponent`; an absolute URL (`https:`, `mailto:`) always renders a plain `<a>`. Without a provider, or without `linkComponent`, internal links are plain `<a>` elements too, so they work but load the page.

React Router's `Link` takes `to`, so it needs the adapter in the example, which maps `href` to `to`. Wrap the app once, in the root route.

In Next.js, `next/link`'s `Link` takes `href` and needs no adapter, but a Server Component can't pass `Link`, a function, to a client component: render the provider from a client file, `app/providers.tsx` in the example, and wrap the app in it from `app/layout.tsx`, which stays a Server Component.

## Props

Type: `OuroProviderProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `children` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | Your app, or the part of it that uses Ouro UI. |
| `linkComponent` | `OuroLinkComponent` |  | Renders internal `href`s, for example an adapter around a router's `Link`. |
| `motion` | `"full" \| "system" \| "reduced"` | `"system"` | How much Ouro UI moves, for an app with a motion setting of its own. `system` follows the device's reduced-motion setting, as Ouro UI does without a provider. `reduced` moves as if that setting were on, whatever the device says: springs settle at once, scrolls jump, and a moment or an emoji holds still. `full` keeps that motion running even where the device asks for less. Ouro UI's motion in script reads it, as does `useReducedMotion` for your own. A provider that sets it wraps its children in an element with `data-motion` set to it (and `display: contents`, so it adds no box), so your CSS can follow the setting too, beside the `prefers-reduced-motion` media query: `[data-motion="reduced"] .wave { animation: none }`. While a provider with `reduced` is on the page, Ouro UI's CSS animations and transitions, and your own, end at once everywhere but inside a provider set to `full`; with `full`, a transition Ouro UI keeps for `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` still follows the device. A provider inside another keeps the outer one's setting when it sets none. |
| `portalContainer` | `HTMLElement \| RefObject<HTMLElement \| null> \| null` |  | The element floating popups render into: the lists of `Select` and `Combobox`, and `Menu`, `Popover`, `DatePicker`, `Tooltip`, `HoverCard` and `NavigationMenu`. Unset, they render at the end of `<body>`, outside every landmark, where screen reader users who move by landmark miss them. Pass an element, or a ref to one, inside `<main>` that does not clip what it holds (no `overflow` other than `visible`) and is not inside an element with a `transform`, `filter` or `contain`, which would hold the phone sheets' `position: fixed`. Render it last in `<main>`, after the content, so popups stack over the page; a ref works even when the element comes after a popup that is open at once. A provider inside another keeps the outer one's container when it sets none, and `null` gives popups Base UI's place again: wrap the content of a dialog that is not Ouro UI's in `<OuroProvider portalContainer={null}>` so its popups open inside it. Dialogs, sheets and toasts stay at the end of `<body>`: a dialog is announced when it opens, and the toasts are a landmark of their own. |

## Types

### `OuroLinkComponent`

A component that renders an internal link, such as a router's `Link`.

```ts
type OuroLinkComponent = ComponentType<
  AnchorHTMLAttributes<HTMLAnchorElement> & { href: string; ref?: Ref<HTMLAnchorElement> }
>;
```
